ground_truth.description: The test's local `_shape_task` helper copies the recency key from `task.get('updated_at')` (snake_case), whereas production `tasks.py:_shape_task` reads `task.get('updatedAt')` (camelCase, the actual MCP/Taskmaster field name). The three new tests feed already-snake_cased fake tasks, so they exercise the max/None logic but never validate the real camelCase→snake_case conversion; a regression in that field mapping would silently make `last_update` always None and go uncaught.

A six-line inline comment above last_update defends the lexicographic max, names a rejected alternative and a scope rationale; it relies on an unenforced cross-package invariant (updatedAt always written by fused-memory sqlite_task_backend._now as UTC 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.mmmZ') and its last line ('flatten the task tree first') is misleading since tasks._shape_task drops subtasks. The max itself is correct today.

The task's user-observable signal is 'updated 4m ago', but DF_SHELL.timeago returns a bare unit ('4m'), so OrchTab renders 'Updated · 4m' and the overview renders '4m' under an 'Updated' header. The '—' empty state is met by timeago itself.

Neither new render site (tab_overview.jsx Updated column, tabs.jsx 'Updated ·' line) is covered by the repo's existing text-wiring JSX tests, so removing or misnaming timeago(o.last_update) would not be caught.

The new last_update tests use naive '2026-06-12T15:30:00' values instead of the production 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.mmmZ' format, and no case covers an empty-string updated_at (the backend COALESCEs NULL to '').

The three new last_update tests repeat identical setup (function-local imports, config, find_running_orchestrators patch, discover call, length assert), differing only in the task list and expected value.

In the ORCHESTRATORS payload the sibling 'started' field encodes absence as '' while the new 'last_update' passes None through, giving two absent encodings for timestamp-like fields; both render as '—' today only because timeago treats any falsy value alike.
discover_orchestrators' docstring lists the enrichment keys it attaches (tasks, worktrees, summary) but was not updated for the new derived 'last_update' key.

task.title: Dashboard Orchestrators panel: per-orchestrator last-update timestamp
task.description:
Add a per-orchestrator "last update" timestamp to the dashboard Orchestrators section so a viewer can distinguish a progressing orchestrator from a stalled one (today only the process `started` time is shown).

Implementation:
- In `discover_orchestrators()` (dashboard/src/dashboard/data/orchestrator.py, ~line 300 where `summary` is built and `tasks` is in scope), compute `last_update = max(t['updated_at'] for t in tasks if t.get('updated_at'))`, or `None` when no task carries `updated_at`. Add `'last_update'` to the per-orchestrator result dict (sibling of `summary`/`started`).
- In `shape_orchestrators()` (dashboard/src/dashboard/data/redux_api.py, ~line 53), copy it onto each ORCHESTRATORS entry as a sibling of `'started'`: `'last_update': o.get('last_update')`.
- Render in `OrchTab` (dashboard/src/dashboard/static/redux/tabs.jsx) and the overview row (dashboard/src/dashboard/static/redux/tab_overview.jsx) as a relative time ("updated 4m ago"); show "—" when `last_update` is absent. Reuse an existing JS time-format helper in static/redux/ if one exists, else add a small local one (tactical — PRD Open question 1).

Substrate: tasks already carry `updated_at` (preserved from `updatedAt` at data/tasks.py:66; recency key in data/active_tasks.py). Backend ships the raw ISO string; frontend formats (matches the existing raw-`started` pattern). Empty → "—" (no synthetic data).

PRD: plans/dashboard-orch-update-and-fm-uptime-prd.md task α
Capability manifest: plans/dashboard-orch-update-and-fm-uptime.capability-manifest.md

User-observable signal: An orchestrator row in the Orchestrators tab AND the overview panel shows "updated <relative> ago" reflecting its most recently updated task; "—" when the tree has no dated tasks.
Consumer: dashboard operator (Orchestrators tab + overview panel).
Modules touched: dashboard
